samples: This module manages a small SQLite-backed inventory table, creating it if needed, updating stock when deliveries arrive, and reporting items whose quantity is at or below their reorder level. Its main entry point is tailored to a fixed database file and a specific delivery for one SKU, then prints any remaining low-stock items to the console. Use it if you need a simple local inventory/reorder tracker, but expect to adapt the hardcoded delivery details for general use.

This module manages a small SQLite-backed inventory: it opens or creates the items table, records deliveries by increasing an item’s quantity, and reports products whose quantity is at or below their reorder level. Its main program uses a fixed database path and records a hard-coded delivery of 500 units for SKU BOLT-10 before printing all remaining low-stock items. Use it as a simple stock/reorder helper, but expect failures if the database operation fails or the delivered SKU does not exist.

This module manages a small SQLite-backed stock inventory: it opens/initializes an items table, records deliveries by increasing quantity for an existing SKU, and reports items whose quantity is at or below their reorder level. Its main entry point uses `data/inventory.db`, records a delivery of 500 units for SKU `BOLT-10`, then prints any remaining low-stock items. Use it if you need a simple local inventory/reorder tracker and are comfortable with the hardcoded delivery behavior or plan to adapt it.

This program manages a small SQLite-backed inventory database, creating the items table if needed. It can record a delivery for an existing SKU and report items whose quantity is at or below their reorder level, sorted by lowest stock first. Its main run updates `BOLT-10` by 500 units, then prints any remaining items that need reordering.

This program is a small SQLite-backed inventory tool: it opens or initializes an items table, records a delivery for a specific SKU, then lists products whose stock is at or below their reorder level. Its built-in main flow is hardcoded to add 500 units to the BOLT-10 item in a local database and print any remaining low-stock items, failing if the SKU does not exist or the database operation fails. A test verifies that after replenishing BOLT-10, only the still-low item is reported.
